grammar: verb, aorist subjunctive active, 3rd person plural

μέχρι ὑμῶν συνήσω: I will attend as far as you; ὑμῶν is the object of the preposition, not a possessive.

τοιούτων refers to the locusts and flies, not deeds.
εἰς ὑπόμνησιν is purpose, for a reminder.
τῶν λογίων is a genitive after ὑπόμνησιν, reminder of the oracles.
τῆς σῆς εὐεργεσίας is a genitive of separation with ἀπερίσπαστοι, cut off from your kindness.
σός is attributive to λόγος, your word.
ὁ is an attributive article after λόγος of the same case.
ζωῆς is a genitive with ἐξουσίαν, authority of life and death.
ᾅδου is a genitive after πύλας, gates of Hades.
τῇ κακίᾳ is an instrumental dative, kills by his wickedness.
ἀναστρέφει has the man as subject and the spirit as object, he does not bring back.
ἀναλύει is to set free, release the soul taken.
βραχίονος is a genitive after ἰσχύϊ, strength of your arm.
ξένοις ὑετοῖς is an instrumental dative, flogged with strange rains.
πυρί is an instrumental dative with καταναλισκόμενοι.
δικαίων is a genitive with ὑπέρμαχος, defender of the righteous.
Θεοῦ is a genitive with κρίσει, the judgment of God.
κρίσει is an instrumental dative with ἐλαύνονται.
the subject of διαφθείρῃ is the fire, it, not he.
ἀγγέλων is a genitive with τροφήν, food of angels.
a gloss holds a stray full stop.

grammar: present active participle, accusative masculine singular; substantival
note: ἰσχύοντα is a participle agreeing with ἄρτον, having power for every delight, not a strong man.
ὑπόστασις here is your substance, the food you gave, not support.
τῇ ἐπιθυμίᾳ is the dative with ὑπηρετῶν, serving the desire.
τοῦ with the participle προσφερομένου carries the noun, of the one partaking.

grammar: present middle/passive participle, genitive masculine singular
note: the article at position 14 carries of the one, so it is not doubled.
ὑπέμεινε πῦρ is endured the fire, not remained.
ἐπιλελῆσθαι is the perfect infinitive of ἐπιλανθάνομαι, to forget.
τῶν with the participle πεποιθότων after ὑπέρ carries the noun.
εἰς σὲ πεποιθότων is those who trust in you.

grammar: perfect active participle, genitive masculine plural
note: the article at position 19 now carries those, so the participle must not repeat it.
τῇ δωρεᾷ is the dative with ὑπηρέτει, served your gift.
ὑπηρέτει is an imperfect, past, with τότε.
ὅτι after μάθωσιν gives what they learn, that.
τούς with the participle πιστεύοντας carries the noun.

grammar: present active participle, accusative masculine plural
note: the article at position 21 now carries those, so it is not doubled.
ὑπὸ πυρός with a passive participle gives the agent, by fire.
πυρός follows ὑπό, so it takes no extra of.
ἁπλῶς is simply, merely; intact is a wrong sense.
σου is an objective genitive, thanksgiving to you, not your thanksgiving.
πρὸς ἀνατολήν here is at the rising of light.
φωτός is a genitive after ἀνατολήν, rising of light.
ἀχαρίστου is a genitive with ἐλπίς, the hope of the ungrateful.
σκότους is a genitive after δέσμιοι, prisoners of darkness.
νυκτός is a genitive after πεδῆται, fettered by a long night.
τῆς προνοίας is a genitive of separation after φυγάδες, exiles from providence.
κρυφαίοις is an adjective agreeing with ἁμαρτήμασιν, hidden sins.
λήθης is a genitive with παρακαλύμματι, covering of forgetfulness.
παρακαλύμματι is a dative, under a lightless covering.
ἰνδάλμασιν is an instrumental dative with ἐκταρασσόμενοι.
οὐδέ is the conjunction nor, not even, not the pronoun not one.
the subject of διεφύλασσεν is μυχός, the recess, not he.
ἄστρων is a genitive with φλόγες, flames of stars.
τῆς ὄψεως is a genitive of comparison after χείρω, worse than that unseen sight.
μή negates θεωρουμένης; unseen with being seen doubles the idea.
μαγικῆς τέχνης is a genitive after ἐμπαίγματα, mockeries of magic art.
τῆς ἀλαζονείας is a genitive after ἔλεγχος, rebuke of the boastfulness.
οἱ with the participle ὑπισχνούμενοι carries the noun.

grammar: present middle participle, nominative masculine plural
note: the article at position 1 carries those, so the participle takes who.
κνωδάλων is a genitive after παρόδοις, passings of wild creatures.
παρόδοις is an instrumental dative with ἐκσεσοβημένοι.
ἑρπετῶν is a genitive after συριγμοῖς, hissings of reptiles.
συριγμοῖς is an instrumental dative with ἐκσεσοβημένοι.

grammar: adverb from neuter accusative singular of μήθω (to learn) + ἀπό (from)
note: μηθαμόθεν is from nowhere, as Athens μηδαμόθεν; learning is a misreading.
τῇ συνειδήσει is an instrumental dative with συνεχομένη, pressed by conscience.
τῆς αἰτίας is a genitive of comparison after πλείονα, greater than the cause.
οἱ with the participle κοιμώμενοι carries the noun, those sleeping.
τὰ μέν ... τὰ δέ is adverbial, partly ... partly.
τὰ μέν ... τὰ δέ is adverbial, partly ... partly.
φαντασμάτων is a genitive after τέρασιν, marvels of apparitions.
τῆς ψυχῆς is a genitive with προδοσίᾳ, failure of the soul.
προδοσίᾳ is an instrumental dative with παρελύοντο.
ἐπῆλθεν is an aorist, past.
οὖν completes ὃς δήποτ᾿ οὖν, whoever then; at the time is a wrong sense.
εἴ τε is the split εἴτε, whether, as Athens prints.
τε is the second half of the split εἴτε, glossed at position 1.
τῶν agrees with μόχθων, a worker of the toils in the desert.

grammar: cardinal accusative feminine singular, object understood
note: μίαν is the second half of the split word ἐρημίαν, glossed at position 12.
ἔμενεν with the object ἀνάγκην is awaited the necessity, not remained.
μιᾷ ἁλύσει is an instrumental dative with ἐδέθησαν, bound with one chain.
σκότους is a genitive after ἁλύσει, chain of darkness.
ὀρνέων is a genitive with ἦχος, sound of birds.

grammar: present active participle plural genitive neuter or masculine
note: καταρριπτομένων is passive and agrees with πετρῶν, rocks thrown down.
πετρῶν is a genitive with κτύπος, crash of rocks.

grammar: Noun, feminine gender, genitive case, plural, superlative degree
note: κοιλοτάτων follows ἐκ and agrees with ὀρέων, so it takes no of.
καταλάμπετο is passive, as Athens κατελάμπετο, the world was lit with light.
ἀνεμποδίστοις ἔργοις is a dative with συνείχετο, occupied with unhindered works.

grammar: relative pronoun, genitive neuter plural, part of 'because'
note: ὧν is a relative pronoun, whose voice they heard, not an article to leave out.
φιλοτίμου ξενιτείας is a genitive after ἥλιον, a sun of a glorious sojourn.
φωτός is a genitive of separation with στερηθῆναι, deprived of light.
οἱ with the participle φυλάξαντες carries the noun.
δι᾿ ὧν with the genitive is through whom.

grammar: relative pronoun, attracted to its antecedent, genitive neuter plural
note: ὧν refers to your sons, through whom.
τῷ αἰῶνι is the dative indirect object of δίδοσθαι.
εἰς ἔλεγχον is purpose, for a reproof.
ἔλεγχος is a reproof or conviction, not punishment.
ἀφείλω is an aorist statement, not a question.
τέκνων is a genitive after πλῆθος, multitude of children.
πατράσιν is a dative with προεγνώσθη, made known to our fathers.
ὑπό with the genitive after a passive gives the agent.

grammar: substantival adjective nominative masculine plural in address
note: ὅσιοι is an adjective agreeing with παῖδες, holy children.
ἀγαθῶν is a genitive after παῖδες, children of good people.
τῶν αὐτῶν with the article is the same, not their.
πατέρων is a genitive with αἴνους, songs of praise of the fathers.
ἐχθρῶν is a genitive with βοή, cry of enemies.
ἅμα δεσπότῃ is together with the master.
βασιλεῖ is a dative with τὰ αὐτά, the same as the king.
τά is the article of τὰ αὐτά.
αὐτά after the article is the same, the same things.
οὐδέ is the conjunction nor, not the pronoun not one.
ἱκανοί is sufficient, enough to bury them.
ἐπεί here is causal, since.
πρὸς μίαν ῥοπήν is in one moment.
φαρμακείας is sorceries, as Athens has it.
Θεοῦ is a genitive with υἱόν, son of God.
τάχει is from τάχος, speed, not course.
βασιλειῶν is an accent misprint for βασιλείων, royal thrones, as Athens reads it.
ἀνυπόκριτον is unfeigned, sincere, not unfailing.
θανάτου is a genitive of content after ἐπλήρωσε, filled with death.
ὀνείρων is a genitive after φαντασίαι, visions of dreams.
θανάτου is a genitive after πεῖρα, experience of death.
πλήθους is a genitive after θραῦσις, destruction of the multitude.
ἐπὶ πολύ is for long.
τὸ ... ὅπλον has the article at position 6, so a contradicts it.
θυμιάματος is a genitive with ἐξιλασμόν, atonement of incense.
ἐστι is third person, that he is your servant.
τοῦ σώματος is a genitive after ἰσχύϊ, strength of the body.
ὅπλων is a genitive with ἐνεργείᾳ, activity of weapons.
ἐνεργείᾳ is an instrumental dative parallel to ἰσχύϊ.
πατέρων is a genitive after ὅρκους, oaths of the fathers.

grammar: perfect active participle, genitive masculine plural; substantival
note: πεπτωκότων is a genitive absolute participle agreeing with νεκρῶν, so those doubles the noun.

grammar: aorist active participle, nominative masculine singular
note: στάς is singular, the blameless man standing between.
ποδήρους is an adjective agreeing with ἐνδύματος, so robe doubles the noun.

grammar: present active participle, nominative masculine singular
note: ὁ ὀλοθρεύων is a substantival participle, the destroyer.
τῆς ὀργῆς is a genitive after πεῖρα, experience of the anger.
the article τοῖς at position 1 already carries to the, so the is doubled.
ἀνοίας is a genitive after λογισμόν, a thought of folly.
ἐπὶ τοῦτο τὸ πέρας is drawn to this end.
τῶν συμβεβηκότων is an objective genitive with ἀμνηστίαν, forgetfulness of what had happened.
ταῖς βασάνοις is a dative, the punishment lacking to the torments.
κόλασιν is the accusative object of the verb, so it takes no in.
ξένον is an adjective agreeing with θάνατον, a strange death; enemies is a wrong word.
ἄνωθεν already has anew at position 9, so anew is doubled.
ἐπιταγαῖς is the dative object of ὑπηρετοῦσα, serving your commands.
ξηρᾶς is an adjective agreeing with γῆς, emergence of dry land.
πανεθνί is an adverb, with the whole people.
τόν with the substantival participle ῥυόμενον carries the noun, as Athens has it.

grammar: aorist passive participle neuter accusative singular
note: ῥυόμενον is a middle participle, the one who rescues them, not passive.
ἔτι with the past is still, they still remembered.
τῶν ἐν τῇ παροικίᾳ is a substantival article, the things in their sojourn.
γενέσεως follows ἀντί, so it takes no extra of.
ἐξήγαγεν ἡ γῆ is the land brought forth.
σκνῖπα is gnats, as Athens σκνῖφας.
βατράχων is a genitive after πλῆθος, multitude of frogs.
εἶδον here is third person plural, they saw.
ὀρνέων is a genitive after γένεσιν, a brood of birds.
ὅτι is one letter off ὅτε, when, which Athens prints and the context needs.
ἐπιθυμίᾳ is an instrumental dative with προαχθέντες.
τρυφῆς is a genitive after ἐδέσματα, foods of delight.

grammar: perfect active participle, genitive neuter plural
note: προγεγονότων is attributive to τεκμηρίων, so things doubles the noun.
τῇ βίᾳ is an instrumental dative, by the violence.
βίᾳ is the noun violence, not an adjective.
τῶν κεραυνῶν is a genitive after βίᾳ, violence of the thunderbolts.
οἱ μέν is the pronoun use of the article, those.
τις agrees with ἐπισκοπή, some reckoning.
ἐπεί here is causal, since.
τούς with the participle μετεσχηκότας carries the noun.
τῶν αὐτῶν with the article is the same rights, not their.
ἐπὶ ταῖς θύραις is at the doors.
ἀχανεῖ σκότει is an instrumental dative with περιβληθέντες.
τῶν θυρῶν is a genitive after δίοδον; the article carries of the.
the article at position 17 now carries of the, and θυρῶν is plural.
τοῦ ῥυθμοῦ is a genitive after ὄνομα; the article carries of the.
the article at position 11 now carries of the, so of is not doubled.
AD has no ἐν; ἤχῳ is a locative dative, remaining in sound.
μετέβαινεν ἐπὶ γῆς is went over onto land; over is doubled with crossed over.
ὕδατι is singular.
δυνάμεως is the noun the quenching refers to, the quenching power.
ἀμβροσίας τροφῆς is a genitive after γένος, kind of ambrosial food.
ἐμεγάλυνας is an aorist, past.
τῶν ἄλλων is still governed by διά like the law and the prophets, so no 'of' belongs here.
τῶν is the attributive article of the participle ἠκολουθηκότων after a noun of the same case, not a copula.

grammar: elided preposition with the accusative of direction
note: κατ᾿ αὐτούς with ἠκολουθηκότων means following after them, not in them.

grammar: present active participle, accusative neuter singular
note: δέον ἐστίν is 'it is necessary'; the gloss doubled the verb already carried by ἐστίν.
ἐστίν completes δέον ('it is necessary'); the subject moves here from the participle gloss.
αὐτοὺς τοὺς ἀναγινώσκοντας is intensive: the readers themselves.

grammar: present active participle, accusative neuter singular
note: δέον ἐστίν is 'it is necessary'; the gloss doubled the verb already carried by ἐστίν.
ἐστίν completes δέον ('it is necessary').
τοῖς ἐκτός is dative: useful to those outside; the case relation was lost.
τι τῶν ... ἀνηκόντων is partitive genitive: something of the things pertaining.
τούτων is the genitive complement of ἔνοχοι, those bound to these things.
ἔνοχοι with the genitive here describes learners bound up in these studies, not legal liability.
τισὶ τῶν λέξεων is partitive: in some of the expressions.
Anarthrous αὐτά is the pronoun subject, not τὰ αὐτά 'the same things'.
εἰς ἑτέραν γλῶσσαν with μεταχθῇ is motion into another tongue.
τῶν βιβλίων is genitive after the head τὰ λοιπά: the rest of the books.
Εὐεργέτου is the royal surname of the Ptolemy, a proper name kept in its familiar form Euergetes.
παιδείας is genitive dependent on ἀφόμοιον: a copy of no small instruction.
ἀφόμοιον is the object of εὑρών, a substantive 'copy, likeness', not the adjective 'similar'.
προσενέγκασθαι is aorist middle of προσφέρω, to bring or apply (diligence), misread as from ἀναγκάζω.
τοῦ χρόνου is genitive after διαστήματι: the interval of the time.

grammar: present middle participle, dative masculine plural
note: βουλομένοις is attributive to τοῖς (already 'to those'); the gloss doubled 'those'.
ὑετοῦ is a genitive after σταγόνας; the 'of' relation was lost.
οὐρανοῦ is a genitive after ὕψος; the 'of' relation was lost.
γῆς is a genitive after πλάτος; the 'of' relation was lost.
σοφίας is a genitive after πηγή; the 'of' relation was lost.
Θεοῦ is a genitive after λόγος; the 'of' relation was lost.
ῥίζα is singular.
σοφίας is a genitive after ῥίζα; the 'of' relation was lost.
σοφίας is a genitive after ἐπιστήμη; the 'of' relation was lost.
πάσης is governed by μετά; no extra 'of' after a preposition.
πιστῶν is governed by μετά; no extra 'of' after a preposition.
σοφίας is a genitive after πλησμονή; the 'of' relation was lost.
γεννήματα here are the yields filling the storehouses, not offspring.
σοφίας is a genitive after ῥίζα; the 'of' relation was lost.
AD prints φοβεῖσθε for the infinitive φοβεῖσθαι (as Athens has, an itacism misprint); the clause needs 'to fear'.
αὐτοῦ refers to the angry man: the sway of his anger, not 'its anger'.
ἁμαρτωλῷ is dative: an abomination to a sinner.
ἐπεθύμησας is aorist second singular; the person was lost.
μή already stands at position 1; the gloss doubled the negation.
ἀνθρώπων is a genitive after στόμασιν; the 'of' relation was lost.
σεαυτόν at position 3 already gives 'yourself'; the gloss doubled it.
συναγωγῆς is a genitive after μέσῳ; the 'of' relation was lost.
δόλου is a genitive after πλήρης; the 'of' relation was lost.
ἐπαγωγῆς is a genitive after καιρῷ; the 'of' relation was lost.
χρυσός at position 5 is the subject; 'it' doubled it.
ταπεινώσεως is a genitive after καμίνῳ; the 'of' relation was lost.
οἱ carries the substantival participle φοβούμενοι (those fearing), as in the next verses.
ὑπομονή is endurance or patience, not hope.
καρδίας is accusative plural.
ἀνθρώπων is a genitive after χεῖρας; the 'of' relation was lost.
ἐμοῦ is the genitive object of ἀκούσατε (listen to me, the father), not the possessive 'my'.
μητρός is a genitive after κρίσιν; the 'of' relation was lost.
ὑπὸ τέκνων with the passive εὐφρανθήσεται gives the agent: gladdened by children.
ἐν τοῖς γεννήσασιν is the sphere of service (to his parents); ἐν does not mean 'as'.
παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ is 'from him'; the possessive 'his' left the preposition without an object.
πατρός is a genitive after ἀτιμίᾳ; the 'of' relation was lost.
πατρός is a genitive qualifying ἀτιμία: a father's dishonor.
πατρός is a genitive after τιμῆς; the 'of' relation was lost.
πατρός is a genitive after γήρᾳ, and σου at position 6 already gives 'your'.
συγγνώμην is the noun object of ἔχε: have forbearance.

grammar: present active imperative, second singular, completes the expression
note: ἔχε is the imperative 'have'; 'with him' was invented and the verb lost.
πατρός is a genitive after ἐλεημοσύνη (kindness to a father); the 'of' relation was lost.
εἶ is second person singular; the subject was lost.
τῶν κρυπτῶν is the genitive after χρεία: need of the hidden things.
τῶν ἔργων is a genitive after τοῖς περισσοῖς; the 'of' relation was lost.
ἀνθρώπων is a genitive after συνέσεως; the 'of' relation was lost.
πονηρά is the adjective agreeing with ὑπόνοια, not a noun 'evil things'.
γνώσεως is the genitive after ἄμοιρος; the 'of' relation was lost.
ἐπαγωγή here is a visitation or calamity on the proud, not 'induction'.
πονηρίας is a genitive after φυτόν; the 'of' relation was lost.
ἀκροατοῦ is a genitive after οὖς; the 'of' relation was lost.
ἁμαρτίας is accusative plural.
μέμνηται is perfect middle with active sense: he is mindful, not 'is remembered'.
πτώσεως is a genitive after καιρῷ; the 'of' relation was lost.

grammar: present middle participle, genitive masculine singular
note: προσδεομένου is an objective genitive after δόσιν: the gift due to one in need.
ἀνθρώπῳ is dative: give occasion to a man.
προσφιλῆ is the adjective 'beloved' predicated of σεαυτόν, not a verb; the gloss also held alternatives.
ποίει with a predicate adjective is 'make (yourself beloved)', not 'do'.
ταπείνου takes τὴν κεφαλήν as object (lower your head); 'humble yourself' added a reflexive.

grammar: present active participle, genitive masculine singular; substantival
note: ἀδικοῦντος is a genitive after χειρός; the 'of' relation was lost.
ὀρφανοῖς is dative: be as a father to orphans.
Ὑψίστου is a genitive after υἱός; the 'of' relation was lost.
ἤ after μᾶλλον is comparative 'than', not 'or'.
εὐφροσύνης is the genitive of content after ἐμπλησθήσονται: filled with gladness.
ἐμπιστεύσῃ is third singular aorist subjunctive, matching κατακληρονομήσει (he will inherit).
The gloss held alternatives; δέ here simply continues the clause.
πτώσεως is a genitive after χεῖρας, and αὐτοῦ at position 11 already gives 'his'.
πονηροῦ is governed by ἀπό; no extra 'of' after a preposition.
σωτηρίας is a genitive after καιρῷ; the 'of' relation was lost.
ποταμοῦ is a genitive after ῥοῦν; the 'of' relation was lost.
μωρῷ is the adjective agreeing with ἀνθρώπῳ.
ψυχῇ is 'soul' (your own inclination); 'desires' belongs to ἐπιθυμίαις later in the verse.
καρδίας is a genitive after ἐπιθυμίαις; the 'of' relation was lost.
ἐξιλασμοῦ is governed by περί; no extra 'of' after a preposition.
καταπαύσει is future.
ἐκδικήσεως is a genitive after καιρῷ; the 'of' relation was lost.
ἐπαγωγῆς is a genitive after ἡμέρᾳ; the 'of' relation was lost.
ταχύς is 'quick, swift' (swift to hear), not 'skilled'.
ἐν at position 7 already supplies the preposition; 'with' doubled it.
αὐτῷ is dative: a downfall for him.
τῷ at position 12 already gives the article; 'a' doubled it.
διγλώσσου is governed by ἐπί; no extra 'of' after a preposition.
ἐχθρῶν is a genitive after ἐπίχαρμα; the 'of' relation was lost.
κτᾶσαι is present indicative second singular; the person was lost.
ὀνειδισμοῦ is a genitive after μάχην, and σου at position 10 already gives 'your'; 'for' was invented.
φίλου is genitive: there is no exchange for a faithful friend; the case relation was lost.
τῆς καλλονῆς is a genitive after σταθμός; the 'of' relation was lost.
γεννημάτων is a partitive genitive after φάγεσαι: you will eat of her produce.
ὡς here is exclamatory: how very rough she is.
τοῖς is the article of the dative ἀπαιδεύτοις.
The article at position 5 carries 'to the'; this gloss doubled it.
ἐμμενεῖ is future.
ἐπ᾿ αὐτῷ is 'upon him'; 'to' was invented after the preposition.
γνώμην is opinion or judgment (my counsel), not an order.
εἰσένεγκον here is the aorist imperative second singular (bring your feet into her fetters), not first person.
ἰσχύος is a genitive after σκέπην; the 'of' relation was lost.
δόξης is a genitive after στολήν; the 'of' relation was lost.
ἀγαλλιάσεως is a genitive after στέφανον: a crown of exultation.
πρεσβυτέρων is a genitive after πλήθει; the 'of' relation was lost.

grammar: verb, aorist imperative active, 3rd person plural
note: ἐκφευγέτωσαν is a third plural imperative: let them (the proverbs) not escape you.
γενέσθαι is an infinitive complement of ζήτει: seek to become.

grammar: negative particle with the prohibitive subjunctive
note: μή ποτε after a warning is 'lest (ever)'; 'not' misreads it.
πόλεως is a genitive after πλῆθος; the 'of' relation was lost.
καταβάλῃς is to cast down (yourself among the crowd), not to bind.
καταδεσμεύσῃς is active, to bind (sin twice), not 'become bound'.
τῶν δώρων is a genitive after πλήθει; the 'of' relation was lost.
Θεῷ is dative: to offer to God Most High.
φίλῳ is dative: nor do the like to a friend.
σεαυτόν at position 3 already gives 'yourself'; the gloss doubled it.
ἕνεκεν at position 4 already gives 'for the sake of'; 'for' doubled it.
ἐν ἀληθείᾳ is 'in truth'; with ἐν already glossed, 'faithfully' is ungrammatical.
ἀνδρί is dative, the indirect object of δώρησαι.
συνετῷ is a single adjective; the gloss carried a parenthetical note.
σοί is a dative of possession: a wife is to you.
σεαυτόν at position 13 already gives 'yourself'; the gloss doubled it.
